value.title: Cross-model review round 4 (close-out) — claude-session-start-adopt
value.note:
SCOPE unchanged across four rounds: read-only on code, writes confined to assets/reviews/, no daemon restarted, no real Claude settings written by this review. Close-out of 7bf3f5f1 against round 3 (5dc1cfae..HEAD). Reviewer seat migrated mid-stream from the legacy daemon to rs; the seat name changed, the reviewer did not.

GATES. Targeted per the PM's scoping: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0, `cargo test -p pij-harnesses -p pij-cli` exit 0 with 133 passed (the PM's figure, reproduced), `shellcheck` exit 0, `cargo fmt --check` exit 0. The new test `foreign_empty_hook_entry_survives_reconciliation` is present and passing. No broad suite rerun, as agreed — the change is three tokens inside one function with no callers outside this module.

PROBE. The out-of-tree property probe was re-run unchanged over all 21 shapes so that a fix aimed at one edge cannot quietly regress the other twenty. All 9 F7/entry-survival shapes pass, all 9 valid regression shapes pass, the 3 invalid shapes still refuse without writing, and the inspect probe still classifies all 4 homes correctly. Nothing moved except the case that was meant to.

AC LEDGER, UNCHANGED AND FINAL: AC1-AC5 all TRUE on evidence generated by this review rather than read from the plan.

STREAM TOTAL: 10 findings raised, 10 closed. 8 fixed, 2 refuted on evidence I re-checked rather than conceded. Nothing open.

value.finding: ROUND 3, NOW CLOSED, and closed without buying it at the cost of the behaviour the guard was there for. `let was_empty = hooks.is_empty();` is captured before `retain_mut`, and the push condition is `was_empty || !hooks.is_empty()`, which is exactly the distinction the old test could not make: an entry that ARRIVED empty is kept, an entry the sweep emptied is dropped. I checked both halves in one shape rather than only the half that was reported, because a one-line predicate change is precisely where a fix can trade one bug for its mirror image. Seeding `[{matcher:keep,hooks:[]}, {matcher:a,hooks:[stale]}, {matcher:b,hooks:[stale]}]` yields `[{matcher:keep,hooks:[]}, {matcher:a,hooks:[current]}]` — the originally-empty foreign entry survives in its original position, entry `b` is still collapsed away rather than left as an empty husk, and exactly one managed command remains. The full 21-shape sweep is unchanged from round 3, so the edge was fixed without disturbing anything around it. The regression test seeds the empty foreign entry FIRST, ahead of the stale managed one, which is the ordering that actually exercises the latch; that is the right seed.
value.receipt: out-of-tree probe: foreign-entry-empty-hooks-array now ok (was FOREIGN ENTRY DROPPED on 5dc1cfae, observed by this reviewer); husk check empty-foreign-plus-emptied-managed → {matcher:keep,hooks:[]} retained and {matcher:b} dropped in one output; full 21-shape sweep unchanged; cargo test -p pij-harnesses -p pij-cli → exit 0, 133 passed including foreign_empty_hook_entry_survives_reconciliation; clippy exit 0; shellcheck exit 0; cargo fmt --check exit 0

value.finding: CARRY-FORWARD FROM ROUND 2, NOW CLOSED. G1 read `pij adopt` while the code had correctly moved to `pij-rs adopt`; it now reads `pij-rs adopt` and also states the success-output and empty-stderr obligations the script actually meets. Worth recording why this mattered more than a wording tidy: today's legacy-daemon shutdown notice independently established that `pij adopt` is an UNROUTED verb served by the legacy TypeScript CLI and never reaches rs. A goal that had kept its original wording would have specified a hook that adopts into a daemon being switched off. The code was right and the document was wrong; the document now agrees.
value.receipt: plan.dd.json goals re-read on 7bf3f5f1: G1 names `pij-rs adopt "$TMUX_PANE" --harness claude`; harness/scripts/claude-session-start-pij.sh:19-28 uses pij-rs for both probe and action; corroborated by /Users/jordanknight/pi-hacking/pij/.harness/temp/legacy-shutdown-notice.md

value.rationale: Verified in both directions from one seed: the originally-empty foreign entry survives in place AND the sweep-emptied entry is still collapsed, so the mirror-image regression a one-line predicate change invites did not happen. The 21-shape sweep is unchanged around it.
G1 now names the verb the code runs. The legacy shutdown notice makes this substantive rather than cosmetic: the old wording described adoption into a daemon that stops today.

FINAL VERDICT — APPROVED, UNQUALIFIED. Ship it. AC1 through AC5 are all true on evidence this review generated: clippy 0, targeted tests 133 passed, shellcheck 0, fmt 0, plus 21 settings shapes driven through the planner from a crate outside the repository. Across four rounds ten findings were raised and all ten are closed — eight fixed, two refuted on evidence I re-checked rather than conceded to. Nothing is open, nothing is deferred, and there is no condition attached to this approval. Two observations for the close-out rather than for the code: every one of the four MAJOR/MINOR defects was found by an instrument that ran the real gate or the real function from outside the crate, never by reading the author's receipts — the clippy failure in particular was invisible to `harness checks`, which was the receipt cited for it; and the last two rounds each surfaced a defect in the FIX rather than in the original code, which is the argument for re-probing the whole shape set after every one-line change rather than only the case that was reported.
